title: Attentional Blink
summary: A rapid stream of consonants contains a digit and, on most trials, the letter X. The learner predicts how second-target accuracy will depend on the gap between the two, runs four slow practice trials and then a block of 25 scored trials, and reads the resulting lag function. Second-target accuracy is reported both over all trials and conditioned on the first target being correct, so the size of that analytic choice is visible. A seeded, simulated worked example reaches every conclusion on the page without running a stream at all.
learningObjectives: Describe the two-target RSVP design and what the lag manipulation varies.
Read a lag function and locate the trough and the recovery.
Explain why second-target accuracy must be conditioned on first-target accuracy.
State what lag-1 sparing is and why it constrains blocking accounts of the effect.
Name at least two accounts of the blink that the lag function cannot distinguish.
interactionTypes: scored block with results withheld until the end
catch trials as a response-bias check
line chart paired with a data table
privacy: No data collected, stored or transmitted; trial responses stay in the browser tab as JavaScript variables and disappear on reload, and nothing is written to storage.
accessibilityNotes: Only a single character changes inside a fixed box - the background, size and position are constant, so there is no large-area luminance change of the kind associated with photosensitive reactions, and no CSS animation or transition is used anywhere. Every trial waits indefinitely for both answers, the block can be stopped between trials, and the worked example reaches every conclusion without running a stream, which is the non-timed route the standard requires. Under prefers-reduced-motion the live region says so on load and points to the worked example. The stream box is aria-hidden while running because a glyph changing every 100 ms cannot be usefully spoken. The lag chart is aria-hidden and paired, inside the same figure, with a six-column table giving trials, first-target accuracy and second-target accuracy both overall and conditioned; the two series differ by line style, marker shape and an inline text label, so no meaning rests on colour. Digit and yes/no response buttons are at least 3.25rem tall. Every control has an accessible name, headings do not skip, focus moves to the results heading, and forced-colours rules are supplied for the stream and both chart series. Usable at 320px and at projector widths with no horizontal page scroll; the wide results table scrolls inside its own container.
readmeTopic: Attentional blink: the shape of the cost over time, and the accounts it cannot separate
simulationNotes: The learner's own trials are real responses, not simulated: 18-item streams of consonants (X, I, O and Q excluded from the distractor set), a digit from 2 to 7 at stream position 5, 6 or 7, and the letter X at lag 1, 2, 3, 5 or 8 after it. A block is 25 trials - four per lag plus five catch trials with no X, which is the check on a yes bias. Item duration is 100 ms by default, with 140 ms and 180 ms offered as gentler rates that genuinely shrink the effect. Practice trials run at 220 ms with immediate feedback. Four trials per lag is far too few for a stable estimate; that is deliberate, stated in the results panel, and the reason the worked example exists. The worked example is simulated with mulberry32 seeded at 20260935: 48 trials per lag plus 40 catch trials, first-target accuracy 0.88, second-target detection given a correct first target of 0.86, 0.48, 0.41, 0.72 and 0.88 at lags 1, 2, 3, 5 and 8, detection 0.15 higher when the first target was missed, and a false-alarm rate of 0.08 on catch trials. Lag-1 sparing is therefore built into the generator rather than discovered, and the results panel, the debrief and the challenge all say so. These numbers are illustrative: they are not norms, not published estimates and not anybody's data. Browser timing is a request rather than a guarantee, so item durations are approximate and the tool says so.
